content.title: About
content.content: Cucumber salad with sour cream is a light dish made from fresh cucumbers sliced thinly and tossed with sour cream, seasoned with salt, pepper, and dill. The sour cream gives the salad a creamy, slightly tangy flavor while the cucumbers stay crisp.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cucumbers are about 95 % water, making the salad very refreshing.
Traditional Russian recipes use plain sour cream (20 % fat), but kefir or yogurt can be substituted.
Dill, a common herb in the dressing, has natural antibacterial properties.
The salad is a summer staple because it requires no cooking and cools the palate.
Sour cream helps absorb the fat‑soluble vitamins present in cucumbers.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The high water content of cucumbers helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Cucumber salad is low‑calorie, making it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cucumbers provide B5 and B6 vitamins, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic effect
items.content: Sour cream contains live cultures that can promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The salad supplies potassium and magnesium, important for heart and muscle function.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Sour cream may trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Excessive salt in the dressing can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Bacterial spoilage
items.content: If sour cream is stored at improper temperatures, harmful bacteria can proliferate.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Cucumbers left at warm temperatures for too long may become a source of salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a snack or side dish with meat or fish. Garnish with extra dill, green onions, or toasted pumpkin seeds for added crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Stir before serving, as the sour cream may separate.

content.title: About
content.content: Onions are a bulbous plant of the Amaryllidaceae family cultivated for its edible bulbs. The bulbs have a sharp aroma, mildly sweet flavor and a crisp texture. Onions are eaten raw, sautéed, caramelized, and used as a base for sauces, soups, and sandwiches.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Onions were domesticated over 5,000 years ago in Central Asia.
There are more than 600 onion varieties, including yellow, red, white, and shallot.
Each layer of the bulb is a modified leaf.
Tearing is caused by volatile sulfur compounds released when the onion tissue is cut.
Onions can be stored in a cool, dry place for up to six months.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Onions contain quercetin and sulfur compounds that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Flavonoids and potassium in onions contribute to lower blood pressure and improved lipid profiles.

items.title: Boosts immunity
items.content: Vitamin C and sulfur enhance immune cell function.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Fiber and prebiotic compounds promote the growth of beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Helps regulate blood sugar
items.content: Sulfur compounds may improve insulin sensitivity.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to onions, manifested as skin rashes or swelling.

items.title: Stomach irritation
items.content: Large amounts of raw onion can cause heartburn or discomfort in people with high gastric acidity.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Sulfur compounds may enhance the effect of anticoagulants, so moderation is advised for those on blood thinners.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Onions can be used raw in salads and sandwiches, sautéed, caramelized, roasted, or added to soups and sauces. For a milder taste, lightly sauté the onion until golden.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store onions in a cool, dry, well‑ventilated area. Avoid sealed plastic bags to prevent moisture buildup. Discard any onions with mold or soft spots.

content.title: About
content.content: Pocky is a Japanese snack consisting of thin biscuit sticks coated with a layer of chocolate or other flavored glazes. It was first introduced in 1966 and quickly became popular both in Japan and worldwide.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The original flavor was chocolate, but today the range includes strawberry, green tea, caramel, and many more.
In Japan Pocky is often served as a sweet stick snack alongside tea.
The name “Pocky” is derived from the English word “pocket,” hinting at its convenient portability.
In 2014 a “Create Your Own Pocky” contest was launched in the US, allowing consumers to propose new flavors.
Pocky frequently appears in photos and memes because of its bright packaging.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Contains carbohydrates that provide quick energy.

items.title: Small amount of protein
items.content: The biscuit and coating supply a modest amount of plant‑based protein.

items.title: Calcium from chocolate coating
items.content: Milk chocolate variants contain calcium, beneficial for bones.

items.title: Antioxidants in cocoa
items.content: Dark chocolate versions are rich in flavonoids, which may support heart health.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The biscuit is made with wheat flour, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Most flavors contain a high amount of sugar, so they should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Chocolate varieties often contain milk, posing a risk for those allergic to dairy.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Pocky is calorie‑dense, and large portions can contribute to weight gain.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pocky is designed to be eaten by hand, breaking off sticks from the package. They can be used as a topping for desserts, mixed into ice cream, yogurt, or baked goods.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place with the package tightly sealed. For longer shelf life, keep in the refrigerator to prevent the chocolate coating from melting.
